messages.subject: GGIR Error in Calculating Wear Time
parts:
Hello,

My name is Carmel and I am a research assistant on a project using the GT3X-BT devices. We tried running some preliminary data and the final report stated that there were more minutes of MVPA than there was minutes of total weartime for a day. I wanted to make sure that my code was correct. 

Additionally, I wanted to gage what cut-points are being used. There is a huge discrepancy in what published studies use, so we were thinking of using counts calculated from this METS equation attached and customizing our cutpoints for each age. Thank you so much for any and all support!

Code:
GGIR(mode=c(1,2,3,4,5),
     datadir="C:\\Users\\Desktop",
     outputdir="C:\\Users\\Desktop",
     do.report=c(2,4,5),
     
     #=====================
     # Part 1
     #=====================
     do.enmo = TRUE,
     acc.metric = "ENMO",
     #=====================
     # Part 2
     #=====================
     data_masking_strategy = 1,
     hrs.del.start = 0,          hrs.del.end = 0,
     maxdur = 21,                 includedaycrit = 4,
     qwindow=c(0,24),
     mvpathreshold = 418/15,
     excludefirstlast = FALSE,
     includenightcrit = 5
     
     #=====================
     # Part 3 + 4
     #=====================
     def.noc.sleep = 1,
     outliers.only = FALSE,
     #      criterror = 4,
     do.visual = TRUE,
     #=====================
     # Part 5
     #=====================
     threshold.lig = 44.8, threshold.mod = 100.6, threshold.vig = c(400),
     boutcriter = 0.8,      boutcriter.in = 0.9,     boutcriter.lig = 0.8,
     boutcriter.mvpa = 0.8, boutdur.in = c(1,10,30), boutdur.lig = c(1,10),
     boutdur.mvpa = c(1),
     includedaycrit.part5 = 10,
     #=====================
     # Visual report
     #=====================
     timewindow = c("WW"),
     visualreport=TRUE)

messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] GGIR Error in Calculating Wear Time
parts:
Hi Carmel,

Can you share a more detailed description of the exact results you found by referencing name of output file, variable names and what values they had?

"mvpathreshold = 418/15," does not seem right but it is only used in GGIR part 2 and maybe not related to your problem but that is hard to say because you did not detail where you observed your problem.

Discrepancies between methods is not a methodological problem but a problem with researchers who expect that different calculations can produce identical output. Using MET classification  does not solve that. Solutions are: Process different datasets with the same algorithm or if not possible, rely on algorithms that are not threshold dependent such as average acceleration, time spent in acceleration ranges with bins to ease compare results, MXLX analysis, and intensity gradient. Some of these still have parameters but at least those parameters tend to be more consistent in the field and easier to overcome.

Best,

Vincent
